foods.kidney_notes: A kidney-friendly protein: 1/4 block is ~7 g protein with ~100 mg phosphorus (plant phosphorus is poorly absorbed); calcium-set brands add calcium.
foods.name: Tofu, firm

foods.kidney_notes: Hard cheeses are high in phosphorus (~130 mg per oz) and salt; 1 oz a day is a common limit, cream cheese is lower.
foods.name: Cheese, cheddar

foods.kidney_notes: Moderate phosphorus (~130 mg per oz); fine in a 1 oz portion.
foods.name: Cheese, mozzarella, part skim

foods.kidney_notes: Processed cheese is made with sodium phosphate emulsifiers (almost fully absorbed) and is very salty; natural Swiss or cream cheese is the swap.
foods.name: Cheese, American, processed

foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~925 mg); the skin is worst. Swap for white rice, pasta, or a small portion of leached boiled potato.
foods.name: Potato, baked, with skin

foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~420 mg); a renal dietitian usually suggests apples, berries or grapes instead.
foods.name: Banana, raw

foods.kidney_notes: Cabbage is renal-friendly, but fast-food slaw dressing adds ~250 mg sodium and sugar; homemade with vinegar is the swap.
foods.name: Coleslaw, fast food

foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~495 mg per cup) and 21 g sugar; apple, grape or cranberry juice are the low-potassium swaps.
foods.name: Orange juice

foods.kidney_notes: 4 fl oz is ~14 g fast carbs and only ~125 mg potassium, which is why apple juice is the usual hypo drink for CKD; a full glass doubles everything.
foods.name: Apple juice

foods.kidney_notes: A cup of milk is ~340 mg potassium and ~225 mg phosphorus; keep to 1/2 cup or swap to unenriched rice milk.
foods.name: Milk, 2% reduced fat

foods.kidney_notes: Dark colas get their tang from phosphoric acid (fully absorbed phosphorus) and carry ~39 g sugar; a clear soda, or sparkling water with lemon, is the swap.
foods.name: Cola, regular

foods.kidney_notes: Pure dextrose with no potassium, phosphorus or sodium: the ideal hypo treatment with kidney disease (rule of 15: 4 tablets = 16 g, recheck in 15 min).
foods.name: Glucose tablet (4 g carb)

foods.kidney_notes: One tube is a full 15 g hypo treatment with no potassium or phosphorus; keep one in every bag.
foods.name: Glucose gel (15 g carb tube)

foods.kidney_notes: AVOID with kidney disease: star fruit contains a neurotoxin (caramboxin) that failing kidneys cannot clear; it can cause hiccups, confusion, seizures and death.
foods.name: Star fruit (carambola)

cases.id: TV-S4 orange juice for a low

lines: If your glucose is below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), take 15 g of fast carbs now. Glucose tablets are the best choice on a kidney diet; potassium never delays treating a low.
Check again in 15 minutes. If you are still below 70 mg/dL, take another 15 g.
Skip chocolate, milk or peanut butter for the first treatment: fat slows the rise in glucose, and protein does not raise it.
If someone cannot swallow safely, do not give food or drink: use their emergency glucagon if they have it and call your emergency number.
Log the treatment afterwards and tick "Used to treat a low". It counts toward potassium, but never toward your meal carbs.

lines: If your glucose is below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), take 15 g of fast carbs now. Glucose tablets are the best choice on a kidney diet; potassium never delays treating a low.
Check again in 15 minutes. If you are still below 70 mg/dL, take another 15 g.
Skip chocolate, milk or peanut butter for the first treatment: fat slows the rise in glucose, and protein does not raise it.
If someone cannot swallow safely, do not give food or drink: use their emergency glucagon if they have it and call your emergency number.
Log the treatment afterwards and tick "Used to treat a low". It counts toward potassium, but never toward your meal carbs.
